title: Massachusetts emergency oral Schedule II dispensing and its follow-up
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 721.060(A) an Emergency Situation waives the requirement to use an electronic prescribing system, so written and oral prescriptions may be issued, but they must comply with every other prescription requirement including 105 CMR 721.070(B). Under 721.060(B) a pharmacist may dispense a SCHEDULE II controlled substance on the written or orally transmitted authorization of a prescribing practitioner provided: the quantity is limited to the amount adequate to treat the patient during the emergency period; the prescription carries everything M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(a) requires except the practitioner's actual signature and is immediately entered into a compliant electronic pharmacy system or reduced to writing; if the practitioner is not known to the pharmacist, the pharmacist makes a reasonable good faith effort to determine the authorization came from a prescribing practitioner; WITHIN SEVEN BUSINESS DAYS the practitioner causes an electronic OR written prescription for the emergency quantity to be delivered, bearing 'Authorization for Emergency Dispensing' on its face, with a mailed written prescription postmarked within the period; and on receipt the pharmacist ATTACHES it to the orally transmitted prescription earlier reduced to writing. The pharmacist SHALL NOTIFY the nearest DEA office if the practitioner fails to deliver it.
exam_relevance: Tests the Massachusetts emergency oral Schedule II conditions and, in particular, that Massachusetts measures the follow-up in seven BUSINESS days where the federal rule measures seven days.

numeric_facts.fact: Practitioner follow-up after an emergency orally transmitted Schedule II prescription
numeric_facts.conditions: Electronic or written; a mailed written prescription must be postmarked within the period

exceptions: The emergency waiver removes the electronic-prescribing requirement only; every other prescription requirement, including 105 CMR 721.070(B), continues to apply.
common_confusions: Reading the Massachusetts seven business days as the federal seven days in 21 CFR 1306.11(d)(4).
Forgetting that the follow-up may be electronic and looking only for a written prescription.
Missing the pharmacist's duty to notify the DEA when the follow-up never arrives.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 721.060 read verbatim in the current official publication dated 9/27/24 on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V5 audit found the Massachusetts emergency oral Schedule II pathway had no canonical home. Independent audit still required.
